answer.rationale: Rollback is blocked by compliance (security patch), and circuit breakers or regional failover risk dropping or rerouting in-flight settlement writes during peak load, conflicting with the objective of not losing customer writes. The symptom pattern—write-path latency climbing under heavy write volume at daily peak—most closely matches memory_b3 (provisioning headroom before a retail peak absorbed surge, kept queue depth flat) rather than a partner-outage or bad-build scenario. memory_b5 is a plausible complementary lever (offloading read/report traffic from the primary could relieve some write-path pressure) but is secondary if the load is dominated by genuine write volume rather than read contention, so I want to verify both before committing capacity as the primary lever versus splitting effort with read-replica routing. Given only one intervention slot, add_capacity is the lowest-risk-to-writes option that directly targets sustained availability under peak load without altering the security-patched release or shifting traffic regionally.
